subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to run-session cleanup, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only contract?
rationale: The current PR and the open strict-validation PR encode conflicting product contracts, and the safest repair shape depends on which contract maintainers want to own for upgrades and future jobs.

options.title: Finish recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted/load or doctor handling for omitted legacy jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation branch around the chosen contract.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close this PR and pursue validation/recovery work that still prevents isolated run sessions from continuing after completion.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new-job default and document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Finish recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted/load or doctor handling for omitted legacy jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation branch around the chosen contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses cron normalization, persisted-state migration, and compatibility policy, where recent history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
